title: Two back-and-forth proof witnesses are assigned to the wrong structure.
details: David Marker, Lectures on Infinitary Model Theory, Fall2013, section2.2, Lemma2.15 proof (PDFp17, one-based) and Theorem2.19 proof (PDFp18). In the former, the comparison is between (M,a) and (M,b), but the proof says that there is d in N; N is not a structure in this lemma. The witness must be d in M. In the back direction of Theorem2.19, the displayed disjunction is indexed by m in M, but the following sentence chooses c in N. Choose c in M with N satisfying the indicated formula, then extend the map M to N by sending c to the given d in N. The preceding disjunction supplies precisely this repaired witness. These are local variable/domain slips; the corrected arguments establish the intended statements. The corpus adoption in `scott-sentences-for-countable-structures` uses the corrected witness domains in the fixed-model and back-and-forth arguments.
